verdict.rationale: Cursor documents admin control over MCP servers: enterprise admins choose which MCP servers users may run from the dashboard. It also offers Run Modes allowlists covering MCP and Fetch calls, and per-project CLI permission tokens that gate shell commands and file access. These cover the core of governing agent tool access. However, the MCP admin control appears only as a single-line claim, and there is no evidence of lead-level control over first-party integrations such as Slack, GitHub or Linear. missing for 10: detailed docs on the MCP admin allowlist, admin governance of non-MCP integrations (Slack/GitHub/Linear/plugins), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: Enterprise admins can control which MCP servers users may run from the Cursor dashboard.
Run Modes control how the Cursor agent runs tool calls, and when Cursor interrupts you for approval
Configure what the agent is allowed to do using permission tokens
Toggle servers on/off without removing them
